n1955fc2eed9.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Raghunath Rao – Regent for the infant Madhav Rao II
Nana Phadnavis – Leader of the Barabhai council
Nana Phadnavis – Ally of Raghunath Rao
Madhav Rao II – Leader of the Barabhai council
n1955fc2eed9.x: Nana Phadnavis led the twelve-member Barabhai council, governed for the infant Madhav Rao II and opposed Raghunath Rao.

n59596b6db5b.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Death of Peshwa Madhav Rao I – 1772
n59596b6db5b.x: Madhav Rao I died in 1772, after which Peshwa control over the chiefs weakened further; Plassey was fought in 1757 and Wandiwash in 1760.

n5d6f97bad89.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Treaty of Bassein
2. Extinction of the Peshwaship
3. Treaty of Salbai
n5d6f97bad89.x: Salbai (1782) maintained the status quo, Bassein (1802) meant subsidiary subordination, and 1818 saw the extinction of the Peshwaship.

n0ba896dec73.s: Who founded the Holkar house of the Maratha confederacy?
n0ba896dec73.x: The Holkar house was founded by Malhar Rao Holkar; Ranoji Scindia founded the Scindia house.

n5f57c2a59d1.s: After the Third Anglo-Maratha War, Baji Rao II was deposed and pensioned at:
n5f57c2a59d1.x: Baji Rao II was pensioned at Bithur near Kanpur; a small Satara state was created for a descendant of Shivaji.

n312c890b897.s: The Nizam, defeated by the Marathas in 1795, blamed his defeat on the neutrality of:
n312c890b897.x: The Nizam blamed Sir John Shore's neutrality, which pushed him to the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798.

nfa2bd5402fc.s: The Sangola agreement of 1750, which reduced the Chhatrapati to a nominal position, followed the death of:
nfa2bd5402fc.x: The Sangola agreement followed Shahu's death in 1749 and consolidated the Peshwa's position.

n9eefdede06e.s: Who invited Ahmad Shah Abdali to intervene, leading to the Third Battle of Panipat?
n9eefdede06e.x: The Rohilla chief Najib-ud-Daula invited Abdali; Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh was an ally.

n7855bcd3e82.s: Who commanded the Maratha artillery at the Third Battle of Panipat?
n7855bcd3e82.x: Ibrahim Khan Gardi led the Maratha artillery, while Sadashiv Rao Bhau was the overall commander.

n5c8c391c0a0.s: Which Peshwa signed the Treaty of Bassein (1802)?
n5c8c391c0a0.x: Baji Rao II signed the Treaty of Bassein; he was the last Peshwa.

n7c43ec83c51.s: The first Anglo-Maratha peace was the Treaty of:
n7c43ec83c51.x: The Treaty of Salbai (1782) was the first Anglo-Maratha peace; Bassein (1802) meant subsidiary subordination.

n276fe96df81.s: Which Peshwa won Malwa and Bundelkhand and raided Delhi in 1737?
n276fe96df81.x: Baji Rao I won Malwa and Bundelkhand and raided Delhi in 1737.

nc0613be513f.s: The First Anglo-Maratha War arose from a succession dispute after the murder of:
nc0613be513f.x: The war arose from the succession dispute after Narayan Rao's murder, when Raghunath Rao turned to the British.

n58b2ee800c0.s: The phrase "strike the trunk, the branches will fall" is associated with:
n58b2ee800c0.x: The phrase is Baji Rao I's, about striking at the Mughal centre; his ideology is expressed as Hindu Pad Padshahi.

n6211077ab0c.s: The infant Peshwa Madhav Rao II ruled through:
n6211077ab0c.x: Madhav Rao II, installed as an infant in 1774, ruled through Nana Phadnavis.

nindian-history-17-12.s: The First Anglo-Maratha War ended with the Treaty of:
nindian-history-17-12.x: The First Anglo-Maratha War ended with the Treaty of Salbai (1782).

nindian-history-17-47.s: In the Battle of Kharda (1795), the Marathas defeated:
nindian-history-17-47.x: At Kharda in 1795 the Marathas defeated the Nizam of Hyderabad.

nc80c0870be6.s: Which Peshwa died soon after the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761?
nc80c0870be6.x: Balaji Baji Rao died soon after the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761.

nc252d18d01e.s: The Mungi-Shevgaon settlement between the Marathas and the Nizam came after the Battle of:
nc252d18d01e.x: Mungi-Shevgaon was a peace settlement between the Marathas and the Nizam after Palkhed.

n97132cc2e66.s: Balaji Baji Rao, Peshwa from 1740 to 1761, was also known as:
n97132cc2e66.x: Balaji Baji Rao was known as Nana Saheb; under him Maratha power reached its zenith, reaching Lahore and Peshawar.

n91a97bb3dbe.s: Which Governor-General rejected the Convention of Wadgaon (1779)?
n91a97bb3dbe.x: After the British defeat at Talegaon, the Convention of Wadgaon forced them to give up their gains, but Warren Hastings rejected it.

nf3c2d27fad5.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: facts carry no dates)
nf3c2d27fad5.s: The Bhakti movement arose partly because ordinary people found which paths difficult?
nf3c2d27fad5.x: The paths of knowledge (gyana) and action (karma) were considered difficult for ordinary people, alongside reaction against ritualism, priestly dominance and caste.

nbcb207b912a.s: Gorakhnath and Matsyendranath were leading figures of which group?
nbcb207b912a.x: Gorakhnath and Matsyendranath were leading figures of the Nathpanthis, Siddhas and Yogis, who criticised caste, ritualism and orthodox religion.

n10f411b24f3.s: Who set up the Chapakudu, common dining for all castes?
n10f411b24f3.x: Palnati Brahmanayudu set up the Chapakudu and treated the Mala devotee Kannama Dasu as his son.

n3eccdc2ffb7.s: The Tirumurai, the 12-book Shaiva canon called the "Fifth Veda", was compiled by:
n3eccdc2ffb7.x: Nambi Andar Nambi compiled the 12 books of the Tirumurai; Sekkizhar's Periya Puranam is its 12th book.

n1ef2d29e5bb.x: Tulsidas wrote the Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi.

nc6eb145c1d5.s: Which of the following is NOT regarded as a root of the Bhakti movement?
nc6eb145c1d5.x: The Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita and Bhagavata Purana are identified as roots of the Bhakti movement; the Arthashastra is not.

n9bed7526948.s: Akkamahadevi was a 12th-century woman saint of:
n9bed7526948.x: Akkamahadevi was a 12th-century woman saint of Karnataka.

n967ebe95361.s: Which text put bhakti at the centre of religion and described a ninefold bhakti?
n967ebe95361.x: The Bhagavata Purana put bhakti at the centre; its ninefold bhakti includes kirtana, smarana and atmanivedana.

n858cb7c45d9.s: Who was the guru of Mirabai?

n9728e976c3d.s: Tulsidas belonged to which branch of the Saguna Vaishnava stream?
n9728e976c3d.x: Saguna Vaishnavas split into Ramamargis and Krishnamargis; Tulsidas, a devotee of Rama, was a Ramamargi.

ncb99e3172eb.s: Who was the only female Alvar?
ncb99e3172eb.x: Andal was the only female Alvar.

nc6ae2807231.s: How many Nayanars (Shiva devotees) were there?
nc6ae2807231.x: There were sixty-three Nayanars, devotees of Shiva, and twelve Alvars, devotees of Vishnu.

n9859b1caec4.s: The Nathpanthis, Siddhas and Yogis made devotional religion popular mainly in:
n9859b1caec4.x: They made devotional religion popular in Northern India; their practices included hatha yoga, meditation and renunciation.

n3e49520c1d3.x: The Tiruvasagam is by Manikkavachakar; Sekkizhar wrote the Periya Puranam.

n8b4eac621bd.s: Modern scholars trace the indigenous roots of the Bhakti movement to the:
n8b4eac621bd.x: Modern scholars emphasise the movement's indigenous Alvar–Nayanar roots and see Islam as influencing mainly its later egalitarianism.

nindian-history-22-3.s: The Bhakti movement challenged caste hierarchy by placing devotion above:
nindian-history-22-3.x: The Bhakti saints placed devotion above birth and status, and that is how they challenged caste hierarchy.

n1af36146437.s: Both the Nirguna and Saguna streams drew upon which Upanishadic doctrine?
n1af36146437.x: Both Nirguna and Saguna traditions drew on the Upanishadic doctrine of Advaita; the movement was essentially monotheistic.

ndbb15c0e7bb.s: The Alvars and Nayanars, who challenged Brahmanical dominance, came from:
ndbb15c0e7bb.x: The Alvars and Nayanars came from different castes, high and low, and challenged Brahmanical dominance.

n2caa39d092f.s: Which of the following best describes the social impact of the Bhakti movement?
o: It brought Hindus and Muslims closer and weakened caste bondage, without ending caste
It strengthened priestly dominance and rigid caste practices
It permanently established Hindu-Muslim unity and abolished caste
It remained confined to one linguistic region and one social group
n2caa39d092f.x: The movement brought Hindus and Muslims closer and weakened caste bondage, but did not achieve lasting unity or abolish caste.

n8f91224f35d.s: The Nalayira Divya Prabandham, the "Tamil Veda" of 4,000 Alvar hymns, was compiled by:
n8f91224f35d.x: The Nalayira Divya Prabandham contains 4,000 Alvar hymns and was compiled by Nathamuni.

nd7a2ca8a25b.s: Veerashaivism reached Andhra through Palkuriki Somanatha and:
nd7a2ca8a25b.x: Veerashaivism reached Andhra through Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya and Palkuriki Somanatha.

nc11ddb3ab74.s: The Bhakti acharyas gave Bhakti a philosophical base in opposition to:
nc11ddb3ab74.x: The acharyas provided a philosophical basis for Bhakti against Advaita and helped open temple worship to lower groups.

n304d9e86eb1.s: Ramananda's principal object of devotion was:
n304d9e86eb1.x: Ramananda worshipped Rama; child Krishna was the focus of Vallabha.

n26996262ffc.s: Which acharya's tradition worshipped child Krishna along with Radha-Krishna?
n26996262ffc.x: Vallabha worshipped child Krishna and Radha-Krishna; Ramananda worshipped Rama, Chaitanya Krishna and Nimbarka Radha-Krishna.

nae9bad9893e.s: Which disciple of Ramananda was a barber by background?
nae9bad9893e.x: Sena was a barber; Kabir was a weaver, Raidas a shoemaker and Dhanna a Jat cultivator.

naadad4053c5.x: Gaudiya Vaishnavism was associated with Chaitanya; Pushtimarga with Vallabhacharya and Sri Vaishnava with Ramanuja.

n03121aec4d4.x: Madhva's main centre was the Udupi Krishna Matha; Ramanuja's was Srirangam, Nimbarka's Brindavan and Ramananda's Varanasi.

n3eb0d0c6ffa.s: Vedanta Parijata Saurabha was written by:
n3eb0d0c6ffa.x: Nimbarka wrote Vedanta Parijata Saurabha; Vallabhacharya wrote Anubhashya, Subodhini and Vedanta Rahasyam.

n53a9452e39f.s: Vedanta Desika is associated with which sub-sect of Sri Vaishnavism?
n53a9452e39f.x: Sri Vaishnavism split into Vadakalai, associated with Vedanta Desika, and Tengalai; both remained Vishishtadvaita.

n1f37f7d1312.s: In Andhra, Sri Vaishnavism was patronised by the Palnati Haihayas and the:
n1f37f7d1312.x: The Velanati Cholas and the Palnati Haihayas patronised Sri Vaishnavism in Andhra.

n3bfb8362e18.s: Pushtimarga, the "path of grace", is also called the:
n3bfb8362e18.x: Pushtimarga is the Vallabha Sampradaya; Vallabhacharya set up 84 Pushtimarg centres.

n2da4d7b7cf5.x: Sriperumbudur was the birthplace of Ramanuja; Shankaracharya is linked to Kaladi and Madhva to Udupi.

nf7526d60e49.s: Vyasa Tirtha, royal guru to Saluva Narasimha and Krishnadevaraya, was a scholar of:
nf7526d60e49.x: Vyasa Tirtha was a Dvaita scholar and author of Nyayamrita.

ne194e409a66.s: Who was the first Bhakti saint to preach in Hindi?
ne194e409a66.x: Ramananda was the first Bhakti saint to preach in Hindi; he replaced Vishnu worship with devotion to Rama.

n1a5cc4eec61.s: Which exponent of monism (Advaita) is regarded as a forerunner of the Bhakti cult?
n1a5cc4eec61.x: Shankaracharya taught Advaita or monism and is described as a forerunner of the Bhakti cult.

n897870cc703.s: Chaitanya at Puri is associated with the reign of:
n897870cc703.x: Chaitanya was associated with Prataparudra Gajapati's reign at Puri.

na0e9dac3a34.s: The Bhakti saints are credited with contributing to the early stirrings of Maratha and ____ awakening.
na0e9dac3a34.x: Besides enriching Hindi, Bengali, Marathi and Gujarati literature, the saints contributed to the early stirrings of Maratha and Sikh awakening.

n44563407803.s: Mardana is associated as a disciple with:
n44563407803.x: Guru Nanak was associated with Mardana; Ramananda with Kabir, Raidas with Mirabai and Vallabhacharya with Surdas.

nf7649a433d5.x: Surdas used Braj Bhasha; Tulsidas used Awadhi and Kabir Sadhukkadi.

nbb94a3e46de.s: Kabir's dohas and sakhis are collected in the:
nbb94a3e46de.x: Kabir's dohas and sakhis are collected in the Bijak; the Sursagar is by Surdas.

nindian-history-80-16.x: Basavanna is linked to Bagewadi, Shankaracharya to Kaladi, Ramanuja to Sriperumbudur and Chaitanya to Nabadwip.

nindian-history-85-14.x: Madhuravijayam is by Gangadevi; Molla wrote the Molla Ramayanam.

nindian-history-80-2.x: Guru Nanak was born at Talwandi (Nankana Sahib); Kabir at Varanasi, Basavanna at Bagewadi and Chaitanya at Nabadwip.

nindian-history-5-7.s: Which of the following Bhakti saints is the earliest?
nindian-history-5-7.x: Namdev (1270–1350) predates Kabir (1398–1518), Guru Nanak (1469–1539) and Mirabai (1498–1546).

nindian-history-5-17.x: Mirabai's life overlapped with Guru Nanak (1469–1539) and Chaitanya.

nca610ee6bb6.s: Surdas was associated as a disciple with:
nca610ee6bb6.x: Surdas was associated with Vallabhacharya; Kabir, Raidas and Pipa belong to Ramananda's lineage.

nc269c5cbdaa.s: Who among the following lived later than Kabir and so could not have influenced him?
nc269c5cbdaa.x: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi lived from 1564 to 1624, later than Kabir.

nd8fd45aa5da.x: Rag Govind is matched with Mirabai, Sursagar with Surdas and Ramcharitmanas with Tulsidas.

n2b5127172f8.x: Kabir is paired with Sikandar Lodi; Guru Nanak with Babur and Tulsidas and Surdas with Akbar.

n6b3efc75f9e.x: Tukaram was associated with Maharashtra; Vallabhacharya with Gujarat and Chaitanya with Bengal and Odisha.

n89947a3a399.s:
Assertion (A): The Bhakti traditions did not uniformly uphold Brahmanical dominance.
Reason (R): Alvars, Nayanars and Basava, and in Andhra Vemana and Potuluri Veerabrahmam, criticised caste distinctions.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n89947a3a399.x: These saints criticised caste and some promoted common dining of all castes, so the traditions challenged rather than upheld Brahmanical dominance.

n301d1d68f9d.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
n301d1d68f9d.x: The Tirumurai is a 12-volume Tamil Shaiva canon compiled between the 7th and 12th centuries and called the Fifth Veda; Alvar hymns were in Tamil.

nbec31ed2274.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched about the Virashaiva/Lingayat movement?
o: Lingayats – Affirmed the theory of rebirth
nbec31ed2274.x: The Virashaivas rejected caste and untouchability, condemned child marriage, promoted widow remarriage and questioned rebirth.

n952d951c8b4.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: facts carry no dates)
n952d951c8b4.s: Which work of Palkuriki Somanatha is regarded as the first Telugu satakam with all satakam features?
n952d951c8b4.x: Somanatha's Vrushadhipa Satakam is the first Telugu satakam with all satakam features; his Basava Puranam spread Basava's teachings in simple Telugu.

n63a123223a0.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: facts carry no dates)
n63a123223a0.s: Who recovered and edited Annamacharya's sankirtanas preserved on copper plates at Tirumala?
n63a123223a0.x: Veturi Prabhakara Sastry recovered and edited the copper-plate songs; C.P. Brown is linked with Vemana.

n93c3771ae8d.s: The Anubhava Mantapa, an early 'religious parliament' of the Virashaivas, was at:
n93c3771ae8d.x: The Anubhava Mantapa was at Kalyana; its discourses were compiled in the Shunya Sampadane.

n7d1608e3a26.s: Bhakta Ramadasu (Kancharla Gopanna) used state revenue to rebuild the Rama temple at:
n7d1608e3a26.x: Ramadasu, a Golconda revenue official, rebuilt the Bhadrachalam Rama temple and was jailed by Tana Shah for 12 years.

n4a686a83191.s: Potana dedicated his Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu to:
n4a686a83191.x: The Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu, the Telugu Bhagavata Purana, was offered to Lord Rama; Potana wrote eight of its twelve skandhas.

n9bb76123d22.s: Who held the title Ashtabhasha Kavi Chakravarti?
n9bb76123d22.x: China Tirumalacharya, Annamacharya's grandson, held the title and wrote the Ashtabhasha Dandakam.

ncfa749e2757.x: Ramanuja preached Vishishtadvaita and stressed the worship of Narayana and Lakshmi.

nc4e5032cfe4.s: Who translated Vemana's verses into English as 'Verses of Vemana' (1829)?
nc4e5032cfe4.x: C.P. Brown collected, edited and translated Vemana's verses, published in 1829.

nf2f1e10e0ad.s: Rajaraja I consecrated bronzes of all 63 Nayanmars at:
nf2f1e10e0ad.x: Rajaraja I consecrated the bronzes at Chidambaram; Parantaka I had installed statues of Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar.

nea883232536.s: Kshetrayya is associated with which form of composition?
nea883232536.x: Kshetrayya is associated with padams; Tallapaka is linked with sankirtana.

nee6d6a84a79.s: Vemana's poetry is best known for:
o: criticism of caste, superstition and empty ritual
nee6d6a84a79.x: Vemana criticised superstition, empty ritual, idol worship and hypocrisy and advocated humanism and equality.

na8a5778c29f.x: Nimbarka preached Dvaitadvaita; Ramanuja preached Vishishtadvaita and Madhva Dvaita.

nd4576dda79e.s: The first Telugu Dandakam, the Bhogini Dandakam, was written by:
nd4576dda79e.x: The first Telugu Dandakam was Potana's Bhogini Dandakam.

ne9dc3e1076e.x: Timmakka wrote Subhadra Kalyanam; Molla wrote Molla Ramayanam and Vengamamba Venkatachala Mahatyamu.

n3aeaa0481eb.s: Veerabhadra Vijayam, written at the request of Ivaturi Somanaradhya, is regarded as the first work of:
n3aeaa0481eb.x: The cited accounts regard Veerabhadra Vijayam as Potana's first work, written at the request of his guru Ivaturi Somanaradhya.

n71ad513d6eb.s: Which of the following was a Nayanar saint?
n71ad513d6eb.x: Appar, Sambandar, Sundarar and Manikkavachakar are notable Nayanars; Nammalvar, Andal and Tirumangai were Alvars.

n742f8b12cf6.x: Padakavita Pitamaha, Sankirtanacharya and Harikirtanacharya are titles of Annamacharya.

n5078d24a2c3.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: facts carry no dates)
n5078d24a2c3.s: Which Sufi order was strictly orthodox and opposed Akbar's Sulh-i-Kul?
n5078d24a2c3.x: The Naqshbandis opposed Sulh-i-Kul; the Chishtis kept aloof from the court, the Suhrawardis accepted royal service and the Shattaris absorbed yogic practices.

nindian-history-58-21.s: Baba Farid is also known as:
nindian-history-58-21.x: Baba Farid was called Fariduddin Ganj-i-Shakar; his verses are in the Guru Granth Sahib.

neacc9d16aae.s: The Naqshbandi order originated in Central Asia with:
neacc9d16aae.x: The order began with Bahauddin Naqshband; in India it was associated with Khwaja Baqi Billah and Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi.

nindian-history-51-35.s: The Firdausi order, led by Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri, flourished in:
nindian-history-51-35.x: The Firdausis followed Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri in Bihar; the Suhrawardis followed Bahauddin Zakariya in Multan and Sindh.

n1eca0e711a9.s: Qazi Hamiduddin Nagori belonged to which Sufi order?
n1eca0e711a9.x: Qazi Hamiduddin Nagori was a Suhrawardi, unlike the Chishti Hamiduddin of Nagaur, a disciple of Moinuddin Chishti.

n86c47080dd6.s: Sufism absorbed ideas from Vedanta, Yoga and:
n86c47080dd6.x: Sufism absorbed Vedanta, Yoga and Neo-Platonism while accepting the Quran and the Prophet.

n7b58024d66a.s: Breath control became vital in almost every Sufi order after the translation of:
n7b58024d66a.x: Breath control spread after the translation of Amritakund, the Naqshbandis being the exception.

ncd49bf4d3d5.x: Ali Hujwiri (Data Ganj Bakhsh), considered the first prominent Sufi in India, wrote Kashf-ul-Mahjub.

n48df9208f20.s: The dargah of Gesudaraz is at:
n48df9208f20.x: Gesudaraz's dargah is at Gulbarga; Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki's is at Mehrauli and Haji Waris Ali Shah's at Dewa Sharif.

nb5f55a0615e.s: Who took the Chishti order to the Deccan, at Khuldabad, in the 14th century?
nb5f55a0615e.x: Burhanuddin Gharib took the order to Khuldabad in the 14th century; a migration of Chishtis to Gulbarga followed.

nf0d5d2faf32.s: The doctrine of Wahdat-ul-Wujud is associated with:
nf0d5d2faf32.x: Wahdat-ul-Wujud was associated with Ibn Arabi; Sirhindi represented Wahdat-ush-Shuhud.

ncbeef691a36.s: Which of the following was a Be-shara group?
ncbeef691a36.x: The Madaris and wandering Qalandars were Be-shara; the Naqshbandi and Firdausi were Ba-shara orders.

n8303b288caf.s: Early Chishtis avoided ____, which later Deccan Chishtis accepted.
n8303b288caf.x: Early Chishtis avoided court patronage and state grants, while later Deccan Chishtis accepted grants; they encouraged sama and qawwali.

n785b73ad3b8.x: The Naqshbandis opposed sama, while the Chishtis encouraged sama and qawwali and the Suhrawardis adopted sama and raqs.

n127d4ce1a16.s: Nizamuddin Auliya was a disciple of:
n127d4ce1a16.x: Nizamuddin Auliya, born at Badaun and buried in Delhi, was a disciple of Baba Farid.

nd0ca84f4eb4.s: One derivation of 'Sufi' is from 'suf', meaning:
nd0ca84f4eb4.x: Suf means coarse wool; the word is also explained through safa (purity) and the Greek sophia.

nf206129bf62.s: Alberuni noted similarities between Sufi ideas and the Gita and:
nf206129bf62.x: Alberuni compared Sufi ideas with Patanjali's Yoga Sutra and the Gita.

nindian-history-58-18.s: Which Sufi saint was known as Chirag-i-Delhi?
nindian-history-58-18.x: Nasiruddin Mahmud was Chirag-i-Delhi; Nizamuddin Auliya was Mehboob-i-Ilahi and Salim Chishti Shaikh-ul-Hind.

nc945114f6ee.s: The Baba Fakhruddin Dargah is located at:
nc945114f6ee.x: Baba Fakhruddin Dargah is at Penukonda; the Ameen Peer Dargah is at Kadapa and Gesudaraz's at Gulbarga.

o: a shrine at a saint's tomb
a friend of God or saint
a saint's death anniversary, seen as union with God
ncf5e486069e.x: Urs is a saint's death anniversary viewed as union with God; dargah is the shrine, wali the saint and tariqa the path.

n908f1150420.s: Nizamuddin Auliya, associated with sama and distance from the court, belonged to which order?
n908f1150420.x: Nizamuddin Auliya was a Chishti, in contrast to Sirhindi, a Naqshbandi orthodox critic.

n6ecab3185ac.s: Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki is associated with which Sultan?
n6ecab3185ac.x: Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki was linked with Iltutmish; Nasiruddin Chiragh with Muhammad bin Tughlaq and Firuz Tughlaq.

n29997978a40.s: Jahangir imprisoned Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi at:
n29997978a40.x: Jahangir imprisoned Sirhindi at Gwalior Fort; his letters are the Maktubat-i-Imam Rabbani.

n7b5d22fe7bb.s: Who among the following opposed Akbar's Sulh-i-kul and Din-i-Ilahi, as well as sama?
n7b5d22fe7bb.x: Sirhindi criticised Sulh-i-kul and Din-i-Ilahi and opposed sama and visits to saints' tombs.

n9694f52e55a.s: Which of the following pairs (language – literary association) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Punjabi – Baba Farid's verses in the Adi Granth
n9694f52e55a.x: The Jnaneshwari belongs to Marathi; Bengali is associated with Padavali kirtans.

nfb6b7453326.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the growth of vernacular literature under the Bhakti and Sufi saints?
o: Saints used the people's speech in their teaching
Hindi, Marathi, Kannada and Bengali grew as literary languages
Sufis used Hindavi, Punjabi and Urdu in preaching
nfb6b7453326.x: The saints used the people's speech instead of relying exclusively on Sanskrit, which helped regional languages grow.

n198909d1dac.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: facts carry no dates)
n198909d1dac.s: Which of the following correctly describes a social impact of the Bhakti and Sufi movements?
o: They weakened priestly and Brahmanical dominance
Khanqahs were closed to lower social groups
n198909d1dac.x: The movements weakened priestly dominance and khanqahs welcomed different groups, but caste was not completely abolished.

nindian-history-52-17.s: The Faraizi sect was formed by the followers of:
nindian-history-52-17.x: Haji Shariatullah's followers formed the Faraizi sect; Haridas's the Haridasi school and Dadu's the Dadu Panth.

n8ba17b2e605.s: The Rishi movement is associated with:
n8ba17b2e605.x: The Rishi movement belongs to Kashmir; Dadupanth to Rajasthan and Mahanubhava to Maharashtra.

n35e8725c682.s: Which of the following was NOT shared by the Bhakti and Sufi traditions?
n35e8725c682.x: Both valued the guide-disciple bond, devotion over ritual and vernacular preaching; exclusive idol worship was not common to them.

n7d5d342a6ce.s: Sheikh Nuruddin is associated with the:
n7d5d342a6ce.x: Sheikh Nuruddin is associated with the Rishi movement; Basaveswara led the Lingayat/Veerasaiva tradition.

n0e4404c6e4e.s: Which Andhra saint had disciples like Siddayya (a Dudekula) and Kakkaiah (a Madiga)?
n0e4404c6e4e.x: Veerabrahmam's disciples cut across castes and he admitted women; he opposed untouchability and idol worship.

n8376dc82955.s: Who carried forward the syncretic tradition of Akbar's Sulh-i-kul and Din-i-Ilahi?
n8376dc82955.x: Dara Shikoh carried the syncretic tradition forward, while Ahmad Sirhindi attacked these policies.

n0e64b11abc9.s: The Sant tradition, which blended Hindu and Islamic ideas, included Kabir, Nanak, Ravidas and:
n0e64b11abc9.x: The Kabirpanth and Sant tradition included Kabir, Nanak, Ravidas and Dadu and blended Hindu and Islamic ideas.

n3416cd5d768.s: Which of the following continued despite the Bhakti and Sufi movements?
n3416cd5d768.x: The movements did not end purdah or restrictions on women's public life, and caste inequalities persisted.

n621e0fcca15.s: Hath Yoga, whose techniques some Sufis adopted, was practised by the:
n621e0fcca15.x: Hath Yoga was practised by the Nathpanthi yogis of Gorakhnath's tradition, and Sufis adopted techniques such as breath control.

nfcb9f0701ba.s: In medieval India, many Sanskrit works on music were translated into:
nfcb9f0701ba.x: Many Sanskrit musical works were rendered into Persian; the early Chishtis too were fond of music.

n1205aff2c05.s: Which of the following was NOT common to the Bhakti and Sufi movements?
n1205aff2c05.x: Monotheism, asceticism and religious tolerance were common; idol worship was rejected by the Sufis and the Nirguna saints.

na8d5fb0940b.s: Which music tradition remained closely tied to temple Bhakti?
na8d5fb0940b.x: Carnatic music remained linked with temple Bhakti, while Hindustani absorbed Persian, Bhakti and Sufi influences.

n1763289fc5f.s: Kabir and Nanak criticised the rigid orthodoxy of:
n1763289fc5f.x: Kabir and Nanak criticised the orthodoxies of both Hinduism and Islam and stressed spiritual equality.

n722ea695d1e.s: Which statement about women in the Bhakti and Sufi movements is correct?
o: Women were excluded from spiritual expression in both
Only royal women could express spirituality publicly
The movements gave women room for open spiritual expression
Women were admitted to Sufi orders but to no Bhakti order
n722ea695d1e.x: Both movements created space for women's open spiritual expression; Veerabrahmam also admitted women to his order.

n7319b64aab2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the interaction between Nath yogis and Sufis?
o: It was confined exclusively to temple rituals
Hath-yogic techniques influenced some Sufi practices
Sufis adopted certain yogic meditation practices
n7319b64aab2.x: The interaction involved dialogues, meditation and breath control; it was not confined to temple rituals.

n1f7d0be708f.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: only one dated fact)
n1f7d0be708f.s: Banda Bahadur was executed at Delhi in 1716 by:
n1f7d0be708f.x: Farrukhsiyar executed Banda Bahadur at Delhi in 1716 for refusing to convert.

n7230cbe72f5.s: Ranjit Singh's high court at Lahore was called the:
n7230cbe72f5.x: His high court was the Adalat-i-Ala; the Dal Khalsa was the combined force of the misls.

nd85eb1a0348.s: Which Sufi saint was a contributor to the Guru Granth Sahib?
nd85eb1a0348.x: Sheikh Farid, along with Namdev and Ravidas, contributed to the Guru Granth Sahib.

nd4c6ff35b87.x: Kabir was a disciple of Ramananda, not Guru Nanak; his followers are the Kabirpanthis.

n4079bf126d5.s: Ramdaspur, later known as Amritsar, was founded by:
n4079bf126d5.x: Guru Ram Das founded Ramdaspur; Guru Amar Das strengthened langar and introduced the Manji system.

n2c38d600ac4.s: The original name of Banda Bahadur was:
n2c38d600ac4.x: Banda Bahadur was born Lachhman Dev; he conquered Sirhind in 1710 and made Lohgarh his capital.

nindian-history-58-17.s: Which Sikh Guru organised the 22 Manjis?
nindian-history-58-17.x: Guru Amar Das set up the 22 Manjis.

nindian-history-60-7.s: Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth in:
nindian-history-60-7.x: Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth in 1604.

nf62fa67e36e.s: Which of the following was part of Guru Nanak's teachings?
o: Worship of child Krishna through Pushtimarga
nf62fa67e36e.x: Guru Nanak taught Nirguna devotion, Ek Onkar, Naam Simran and Sangat, rejecting the rituals of both religions.

nce1554bac9b.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the Five Ks of the Khalsa?
nce1554bac9b.x: The Five Ks are Kesh, Kangha, Kara, Kachera and Kirpan; Kirtan is not one of them.

n39e2b288a43.s: Who is regarded as the first martyr Guru of the Sikhs?
n39e2b288a43.x: Guru Arjan Dev is regarded as the first martyr Guru.

nde39090d5bd.s: Which of the following pairs about the Treaty of Tordesillas is correctly matched?
o: Lands east of the meridian – Spain
Lands west of the meridian – Portugal
Reference point of the meridian – Cape of Good Hope
nde39090d5bd.x: The 1494 treaty fixed a meridian 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands, with the east going to Portugal and the west to Spain.

nba3471d6b46.s: Which Portuguese navigator reached Brazil and India in 1500?
nba3471d6b46.x: Cabral reached Brazil and India in 1500 and set up factories at Calicut, Cannanore and Cochin.

nindian-history-87-18.s: Vasco da Gama's final visit to India took place in:
nindian-history-87-18.x: 1502 was his second voyage; his final visit was in 1524.

n3617a8a905d.s: During Vasco da Gama's second voyage (1502), after the Zamorin refused trade, the Portuguese settled at:
n3617a8a905d.x: The Zamorin refused trade, Calicut was occupied, and the Portuguese settled at Kochi.

n0d66cd34dbc.s: The charter of the English East India Company (31 December 1600) was granted by:
n0d66cd34dbc.x: Elizabeth I granted the charter, with a 15-year monopoly between the Cape of Good Hope and the Magellan Straits.

n90c53b5b8c9.s: The French established their first factory in India at Surat in:
n90c53b5b8c9.x: The French first factory was at Surat in 1668; the Dutch began at Masulipatnam in 1605 and the Danes at Tranquebar in 1620.

nb114bb41444.s: Fort William at Calcutta was built in:
nb114bb41444.x: Job Charnock settled at Sutanuti in 1690, the zamindaris were bought in 1698 and Fort William was built in 1700.

nff8536e6e25.s: The Portuguese obtained Diu in 1535 from:
nff8536e6e25.x: Diu came from Bahadur Shah of Gujarat in 1535; Goa was taken from the Bijapur Sultan in 1510.

n426004f9623.s: Which of the following European companies was formed first?
n426004f9623.x: The order of formation was English (1600), Dutch (1602), Danish (1616) and French (1664).

n2a52b3c3648.s: Goa, Daman and Diu were liberated from Portuguese rule in 1961 through:
n2a52b3c3648.x: The Portuguese, first to arrive and last to leave, lost Goa, Daman and Diu in 1961 through Operation Vijay.

n2100220be7d.s: The Marathas captured Salsette and Bassein from the Portuguese in:
n2100220be7d.x: The Marathas took Salsette and Bassein in 1739, though the Portuguese held Goa against them in 1798.

nbcffa209e32.s: Bheemunipatnam in North Coastal Andhra was a settlement of the:
nbcffa209e32.x: Bheemunipatnam was a Dutch settlement; Yanam was French.

n8705729401f.s: Which Portuguese governor reversed Almeida's naval policy and pursued territorial conquest, including Goa?
n8705729401f.x: Albuquerque reversed Almeida's exclusively naval approach and took Goa, Malacca and Hormuz.

naa09d5f0e65.s: Who led the English victory over the Portuguese at Swally in 1612?
naa09d5f0e65.x: Thomas Best led the Swally victory; Hawkins's Surat permission had been revoked under Portuguese pressure, and Edward Terry was Roe's chaplain.

n710e108935c.s: Which of the following pairs about the Portuguese on the Andhra coast is correctly matched?
o: Machilipatnam factory of 1670 – Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah
Machilipatnam factory of 1670 – Abdullah Qutb Shah
Waning of Portuguese influence – Early 16th century
Cause of their decline – Religious tolerance
n710e108935c.x: The 1670 Machilipatnam factory was permitted by Abdullah Qutb Shah; Portuguese influence waned by the mid-17th century as their religious intolerance alienated Golconda.

n7e9cffa1f52.s: Which Mughal emperor captured Hugli from the Portuguese in 1632?
n7e9cffa1f52.x: Shah Jahan took Hugli in 1632; Akbar had granted it to the Portuguese in 1579.

n8bddbdf2556.s: Who was the first Portuguese Viceroy in India?
n8bddbdf2556.x: Almeida was the first Viceroy and won the Battle of Diu in 1509.

n8b192511a0d.s: The Portuguese obtained Daman by treaty in:
n8b192511a0d.x: Daman was obtained in 1559; Bassein in 1534, and Diu was conquered in 1546.

n27820adfb75.s: The Portuguese Cartaz system was supported by convoy arrangements known as:
n27820adfb75.x: The Cartaz system was backed by the Caes convoy system and customs duties, and was used in the Bay of Bengal too.

nacfaa7f5f7a.s: The remains of St. Francis Xavier, who reached Goa in 1542, are preserved in the:
nacfaa7f5f7a.x: Xavier's remains are at the Basilica of Bom Jesus, Goa.

na37ef882e03.s: The Portuguese, the first Europeans to come to India, finally left India in:
na37ef882e03.x: The Portuguese were the last European power to leave, in 1961; 1510 is when Goa was taken.

n518726aebf8.s: Which of the following pairs about the Battle of Bedara (Chinsura) is correctly matched?
o: Result – Dutch moved headquarters to Chinsura
n518726aebf8.x: At Bedara in 1759 the English under Francis Forde defeated the Dutch, who then withdrew to Indonesia.

nbc18497f5ff.s: The Dutch settled at Pulicat with the permission of the:
nbc18497f5ff.x: Pulicat was granted by the Chandragiri king; Golconda gave Machilipatnam. Fort Geldria at Pulicat was the Coromandel headquarters till 1690.

nb02056dc709.s: Who set up the first Dutch factory in Andhra, at Machilipatnam in 1605?
nb02056dc709.x: Van der Haghen set up the Machilipatnam factory in 1605 with permission from Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.

nf8155f9c19c.s: Pulicat was ceded by the Dutch under the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of:
nf8155f9c19c.x: Pulicat was ceded under the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824; the Dutch occupation is dated 1605-1825.

nb92ec789cad.s: Mahe was a centre of the:
nb92ec789cad.x: Mahe was a French centre; Kasimbazar, Balasore and Vengurla were Dutch.

n03b7c9ea530.s: Who wrote the Itinerario, part of the background to Dutch expansion in Asia?
n03b7c9ea530.x: Linschoten wrote the Itinerario, while Cornelis de Houtman reached Bantam in 1596.

n5cd2b92976d.s: The VOC received sovereign powers to wage war, build forts and sign treaties from:
n5cd2b92976d.x: The Dutch States-General granted the VOC powers to wage war, build forts and sign treaties.

nf5c4bf24fe8.s: At the Battle of Colachel (1741), Travancore under Marthanda Varma defeated the:
nf5c4bf24fe8.x: Travancore defeated the Dutch at Colachel in 1741, ending Dutch ambitions in Malabar.

n24d0e62988d.s: Which became the first municipality in Andhra, in 1861?
n24d0e62988d.x: Bhimili became the first municipality in Andhra in 1861; Pulicat was the second English settlement and Visakhapatnam came in 1682.

n1949a716bc3.s: The 1600 charter first gave the English East India Company a monopoly of East Indies trade for:
n1949a716bc3.x: The charter gave a fifteen-year monopoly, later made perpetual; it granted trading rights, not territorial power.

nd55e9fb60de.s: Under Farrukhsiyar's Farman of 1717, the Company's Bengal trade became duty-free for an annual payment of:
nd55e9fb60de.x: Bengal trade became duty-free for Rs 3,000 a year with the right to issue dastaks; Surat duties were waived for Rs 10,000.

n08d1fbc965a.s: Bombay was leased to the English East India Company in 1668 by:
n08d1fbc965a.x: Charles II leased Bombay to the Company in 1668; Francis Day founded Madras in 1639.

na0919967bb9.s: Child's War (1686–1690) was fought between the English East India Company and:
na0919967bb9.x: Aurangzeb crushed the Company in Child's War and pardoned it after it paid a fine.

n4480187b26f.s: The Battle of Buxar was fought in:
n4480187b26f.x: Buxar was fought in 1764, after Plassey (1757) and before the end of Company rule (1858).

nindian-history-33-17.s: Sutanuti, one of the three villages that became Calcutta, was a trading centre of the:
nindian-history-33-17.x: Sutanuti was an English trading centre and a Calcutta base; Batavia was the Dutch eastern centre.

nindian-history-33-15.s: The first permanent English factory in India was set up in 1613 at:
nindian-history-33-15.x: The first permanent factory was at Surat in 1613; Masulipatnam had the first temporary one in 1611.

nc099a1e2c4c.s: Charles II and James II delegated to the Company powers of coining money, exercising jurisdiction and:
o: declaring war and peace with non-Christians
nc099a1e2c4c.x: The delegated powers included coining money, jurisdiction and making war and peace with non-Christians.

nbd7a88eab3b.s: Which English Presidency seat was at Fort St. George?
nbd7a88eab3b.x: Madras was at Fort St. George and Calcutta at Fort William in Bengal; Bombay replaced Surat in the west.

nc3d8a5c1c2a.s: Madras became the first municipality in India in:
nc3d8a5c1c2a.x: Madras was India's first municipality in 1687; Bhimili was Andhra's first in 1861.

n22af524e4f4.s: Which of the following pairs about the Battle of Bobbili is correctly matched?
n22af524e4f4.x: Bobbili was fought on 24 January 1757; Bussy aided Vijayaramaraju of Vizianagaram, Ranga Rao of Bobbili was killed, and Tandra Papayya later killed Vijayaramaraju.

n591ffd178ab.s: Who defeated the French under Count de Lally at Wandiwash?
n591ffd178ab.x: Lally lost at Wandiwash to Eyre Coote.

nccce789efd5.s: Chandernagore joined India through a plebiscite in:
nccce789efd5.x: Chandernagore joined by plebiscite in 1950; the other four enclaves passed de facto in 1954 and de jure in 1962.

n274f24d5f03.s: The French East India Company (Compagnie des Indes Orientales) was founded in 1664 by:
n274f24d5f03.x: Colbert, minister of Louis XIV, founded it in 1664; the French were the last European company to arrive.

nbc0a53ea5fe.s: The only French territory in Andhra was:
nbc0a53ea5fe.x: Yanam was the only French territory in Andhra and is now part of the Union Territory of Puducherry.

n3692e41fae3.x: The other Northern Circars became British in 1768; Guntur followed in 1788.

na725d2e4d44.s: Which treaty of 1754 barred the English and French from interfering in Indian princes' quarrels and led to Dupleix's recall?
na725d2e4d44.x: The Treaty of Pondicherry (1754) required both sides not to meddle in Indian princes' quarrels, and Dupleix was recalled.

n994e574c2e4.s: Which of the following was NOT among the Northern Circars granted by Salabat Jang in 1753?
n994e574c2e4.x: The Circars granted were Mustafanagar (Kondapalli), Eluru, Rajahmundry and Chicacole; Nellore was not included.

n932c03d3a3d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Benjamin Schulz's Telugu Bible was published at Serampore
Serampore College was founded by the Serampore Trio in 1818
The Serampore press printed the first Telugu Bible in India in 1807-1810
Schulz began his Telugu Bible translation in 1727
n932c03d3a3d.x: Schulz's Telugu Bible was completed and published at Halle in 1746-47, not at Serampore.

nb2313a741ca.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Benjamin Schulz begins translating the Bible into Telugu
2. Founding of the Danish East India Company
3. Schulz's Telugu Bible published at Halle
nb2313a741ca.x: The Danish East India Company was founded in 1616; Schulz began the Telugu translation in 1727 and it was published at Halle in 1746-47.

nc8291abdbff.s: Tranquebar, the first Danish settlement in India (1620), lies near:
nc8291abdbff.x: Tranquebar lies near Tanjore on the Coromandel coast; the Danish company was founded in 1616.

nbfc82ce6c37.s: The Swedish East India Company, established in 1731, traded mainly with:
nbfc82ce6c37.x: The Swedish company focused on China and had a negligible presence in India.

nc14184c7e5c.s: The Danish settlements in India are historically important mainly for their:
o: Protestant missionary, educational and linguistic work
role as the first British capital
nc14184c7e5c.x: Danish commercial impact was negligible, but their missionary, educational and linguistic work was important.

n1f312670b5b.x: The Danes left in 1845; the Portuguese arrived first in 1498 and left last in 1961.

nbaff847396f.s: Which European power was the last to arrive in India, in 1664?
nbaff847396f.x: The order of arrival was Portuguese, Dutch, British, Danish and French; the French came last in 1664.

n9bc69206f5a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the European companies' dealings with Andhra weavers?
o: The Dutch, Portuguese and French advanced money to weavers
The Dutch, Portuguese and French generally paid weavers fairly
The English paid weavers more than the other companies
The English demanded high quality, so weavers avoided them
n9bc69206f5a.x: The English paid less while demanding high quality, so weavers avoided them.

nap-history-1-9.s: The Ryotwari system was first introduced in the:
nap-history-1-9.x: Ryotwari was first tried in the Baramahals.

nap-history-9-4.s: Which foreign traveller visited the Andhra port of Motupalli?
nap-history-9-4.x: Marco Polo visited Motupalli; Tavernier was the 17th-century trader who visited the Andhra mines.

n7455fecdc27.s: Bussy obtained the Northern Circars for the French in 1753 through a grant from:
n7455fecdc27.x: Bussy secured the Circars through Salabat Jung's grant in 1753; Muhammad Ali was not the grantor.

nap-history-35-5.s: The Zilla-bandi system was introduced in Hyderabad State in 1865 by:
nap-history-35-5.x: Salar Jung introduced the Zilla-bandi system in 1865; Mahboob Ali Khan issued the Mulki rules in 1888.

nap-history-1-35.s: The city of Hyderabad was founded in 1591 by:
nap-history-1-35.x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah founded Hyderabad in 1591; under him the English got permission for the Machilipatnam factory in 1611.

nap-history-9-7.s: In 1626 the British set up a factory in the Nellore region at:
nap-history-9-7.x: The British factory in the Nellore region was at Armagaon (1626); Masulipatnam was the first Dutch factory in Andhra.

nb4b9b86acd8.s: In the Bobbili War of 1757, Vizianagaram was supported by the:
nb4b9b86acd8.x: In the Bobbili War of 1757 the French supported Vizianagaram.

nca2fe6ab27a.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: facts carry no dates)
nca2fe6ab27a.s: Which export of the Andhra region came from Nagulavancha and Nalgonda?
nca2fe6ab27a.x: Indigo came from Nagulavancha and Nalgonda; saltpetre from Machilipatnam, Narsapur and Pulicat, diamonds from Golconda and Kollur, salt from Pedaganjam and Chinaganjam.

ndd73e0e704c.s: The Dutch subordinate factory at Bheemunipatnam later became a factory of the:
ndd73e0e704c.x: Bheemunipatnam's Dutch factory later became English, and Bhimili became Andhra's first municipality in 1861.

nap-history-8-5.s: Who issued an 'Abhaya Sasana' for the development of trade at Motupalli?
nap-history-8-5.x: Somaya issued an Abhaya Sasana to encourage trade at Motupalli, an important Reddy port occupied by Mallaya Reddy.

n1e1e294db83.s: Which Masulipatnam textile was glazed and became brighter after washing?
n1e1e294db83.x: Chintz was glazed and became brighter after washing.

n1a58765ad5c.s: Along with Machilipatnam, which coastal Andhra town was a ship and boat building centre?
n1a58765ad5c.x: Narasapuram, with Machilipatnam, built ships and boats; Corangi was a Company-era shipbuilding site.

n42aa35e2989.s: Yanam, now an enclave of Puducherry in the Godavari delta, merged into the Indian Union in:
n42aa35e2989.x: Yanam merged into the Indian Union in 1954; the de jure transfer came in 1962.

n669b0d0c669.s: Anwaruddin, Nawab of the Carnatic, was killed in 1749 at the Battle of:
n669b0d0c669.x: Anwaruddin, who had backed the English and lost at St. Thome, was killed at Ambur in 1749.

na00c4bfacd4.s: The First Carnatic War was an extension of the:
na00c4bfacd4.x: The First Carnatic War extended the War of Austrian Succession; France used its Mauritius fleet to take Madras.

n7aa9f452f9c.s: The First Carnatic War showed that the Anglo-French contest on the Coromandel coast would be decided by:
n7aa9f452f9c.x: Naval power proved decisive; the war's political result was nil despite Dupleix's victories.

na89bf9a0c59.s: Who led the French force at the Battle of St. Thome (Adyar) in 1746?
na89bf9a0c59.x: Captain Paradis led about 930 French troops who beat about 10,000 men under Mahfuz Khan, Anwaruddin's son.

n4d940bb54df.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the rival claimants in Hyderabad and the Carnatic?
o: Nasir Jang was the son of Nizam-ul-Mulk
Muzaffar Jang was the daughter's son of Nizam-ul-Mulk
Muhammad Ali was supported by the English after Anwaruddin
Chanda Sahib was the English-backed claimant to the Carnatic
n4d940bb54df.x: Chanda Sahib was the French-backed claimant; the English supported Muhammad Ali.

n513dcd8da25.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First Carnatic War – Fought over Indian political succession
Second Carnatic War – Extension of the War of Austrian Succession
Second Carnatic War – Major French territorial gains on the Andhra coast
Second Carnatic War – Fought chiefly on the Malabar coast
n513dcd8da25.x: The Second Carnatic War centred on Indian succession disputes and brought major French gains on the Andhra coast; the First was an extension of the War of Austrian Succession.

n54b3002e25f.s: In 1751 Robert Clive held Arcot for about 53 days against:
n54b3002e25f.x: Clive took Arcot with about 210 men and held it against Raja Sahib, son of Chanda Sahib.

ne6be5c5bfc4.s: The succession disputes behind the Second Carnatic War were triggered by the death of Nizam-ul-Mulk in:
ne6be5c5bfc4.x: Nizam-ul-Mulk's death in 1748 and Chanda Sahib's release from Maratha captivity triggered the disputes.

na9ae0db66d0.s: Which Maratha chief joined the English during Clive's Carnatic campaign?
na9ae0db66d0.x: Mysore, Tanjore and the Maratha chief Morari Rao joined the English.

nce78755a2a1.s: After the Battle of Ambur (1749), Muhammad Ali fled to:
nce78755a2a1.x: Muhammad Ali fled to Trichinopoly, while Chanda Sahib became Nawab after Anwaruddin was killed.

nbdd3514e3c5.s: Nasir Jang, the English-backed claimant to Hyderabad, was murdered in a plot arranged by Dupleix by:
nbdd3514e3c5.x: Nasir Jang was murdered by Himmat Khan, the Nawab of Kurnool.

n25778915fb0.s: During the Carnatic struggle, the only French base in India was:
n25778915fb0.x: Calcutta, Bombay and Madras were English bases, while the French had only Pondicherry.

n680046922ae.s: The Battle of Chandurti (Condore) near Rajahmundry was fought in:
n680046922ae.x: Chandurti was fought on 7 December 1758; the English took Machilipatnam in April 1759.

nc60c8d60908.s: At Chandurti, Colonel Forde defeated a French force commanded by:
nc60c8d60908.x: Forde, sent by Clive from Bengal, joined Ananda Gajapati's army and defeated the French under Conflans.

n891faa8d48b.s: Count de Lally surrendered at Pondicherry in:
n891faa8d48b.x: Lally surrendered at Pondicherry on 16 January 1761, while Bussy was taken prisoner at Wandiwash.

n2f9924911e6.s: Which French commander was taken prisoner at Wandiwash?
n2f9924911e6.x: Eyre Coote routed Lally at Wandiwash, where Bussy was taken prisoner.

n94e596a6f6a.s: The English victories at Chandurti and Machilipatnam gave them their first foothold in:
n94e596a6f6a.x: Chandurti and Machilipatnam gave the English their first foothold in the Northern Circars, while Yanam remained French.

n7d2e19fc8fe.s: In the Hyderabad succession dispute of the Second Carnatic War, the English backed:
n7d2e19fc8fe.x: The English backed Nasir Jang, son of Nizam-ul-Mulk, and the French backed his grandson Muzaffar Jang.

n9dffdac6477.s: The Treaty of Pondicherry, under which each company kept its existing possessions, was signed in:
n9dffdac6477.x: The Treaty of Pondicherry (1754) bound both companies not to interfere in princes' quarrels and was inconclusive.

nb3942d89f29.s: The Carnatic Wars made the ____ the kingmakers of South India.
nb3942d89f29.x: The wars showed the power of disciplined European infantry and made the English the kingmakers of South India.

ne52e423d7da.s: The Battle of Wandiwash was fought on 22 January:
ne52e423d7da.x: Wandiwash was fought on 22 January 1760; Chendurthi on 7 December 1758, Ambur in 1749 and Arcot in 1751.

n59ae2655bf8.s: Who was the English admiral in the Third Carnatic War?
n59ae2655bf8.x: Pocock was the English admiral and d'Ache the French admiral; the English fleet defeated d'Ache.

na72c87bd1ad.s: The First Carnatic War ended with the Treaty of:
na72c87bd1ad.x: The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) ended the First war and returned Madras to the English.

ndc3ba17a031.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the significance of the Battle of Plassey?
o: It turned the Company from a trading body into a political power
It was a prolonged contest between equally matched armies
Bengal's wealth helped finance the defeat of the French
It is seen as a victory of treachery and political-financial arrangement
ndc3ba17a031.x: Plassey is viewed as a victory of treachery and a political-financial deal, not a prolonged contest between equal armies.

n2fed66948a5.s: Which of the following pairs about the conflict between Siraj-ud-Daula and the English is correctly matched?
o: Fort William – Fortified with the Nawab's permission
Krishna Das – Fugitive given asylum by the English
The French – Refused Siraj's order to stop fortification
The English – Obeyed Siraj's order to stop fortification
n2fed66948a5.x: The English sheltered the fugitive Krishna Das and fortified Fort William without permission, while the French obeyed the order to stop fortifying.

nb0e1263111c.s: After Plassey, Mir Jafar rewarded the Company with the zamindari of:
nb0e1263111c.x: The Company got the zamindari of the 24 Parganas, duty-free trade in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, and a large payment.

n813cdb59500.s: The Black Hole story of June 1756 rests mainly on the account of:
n813cdb59500.x: The story rests mainly on the account of J.Z. Holwell, a survivor; historians doubt the reported numbers.

n1b6485c1984.x: Alivardi Khan, earlier Deputy Governor of Bihar, was succeeded by his grandson Siraj-ud-Daula.

n6166c8dc375.s: Clive's Plassey conspiracy involved Jagat Seth, Omichund and:
n6166c8dc375.x: Clive's deal involved Jagat Seth, Omichund and Mir Jafar.

n1b67f32ed43.s: Which of the following events of 1756–57 in Bengal came first?
o: Recapture of Calcutta by Clive and Watson
n1b67f32ed43.x: Kasimbazar was seized in May 1756, before Calcutta fell (June 1756), its recapture (January 1757) and Alinagar (February 1757).

n6d5ff60bf15.s: Who ruled Bengal immediately before Siraj-ud-Daula?
n6d5ff60bf15.x: The order was Shuja-ud-din, Sarfaraz Khan, Alivardi Khan and Siraj-ud-Daula.

n855baab35ac.s: Under the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), Shuja-ud-Daulah of Awadh paid a war indemnity of:
n855baab35ac.x: Shuja paid Rs 50 lakh and recovered his dominions except Kora and Allahabad, which went to Shah Alam II.

n90e8dcc5db1.s: Who commanded the British forces at the Battle of Buxar?
n90e8dcc5db1.x: Hector Munro commanded the British at Buxar against Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II.

n427ff6c107c.s: After his defeat at Buxar, Shuja-ud-Daulah sought help from the Rohillas and the:
n427ff6c107c.x: Shuja fled and sought help from the Rohillas and the Marathas before surrendering.

n53a03a85f39.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: only one dated fact)
n53a03a85f39.s: Under the Dual Government in Bengal (1765–1772), the Diwani was held by:
n53a03a85f39.x: The Company held the Diwani (revenue and civil justice) while the Nawab kept the Nizamat.

nc6e2a0af6a1.s: Najm-ud-Daula, who became Nawab of Bengal in 1765, was the son of:
nc6e2a0af6a1.x: Najm-ud-Daula was Mir Jafar's son; he held the Nizamat in name only.

n392d0f5e0c0.s: Who was the last independent Nawab of Bengal?
n392d0f5e0c0.x: Siraj-ud-Daulah, the last independent Nawab, was defeated by Clive at Plassey despite French support.

n7bc5af20349.s: Who called Robert Clive a 'heaven-born general'?
n7bc5af20349.x: William Pitt called Clive a 'heaven-born general'; Clive was Governor of Bengal twice.

nb7db73f4097.s: Warren Hastings became Governor of Bengal in:
nb7db73f4097.x: Warren Hastings became Governor of Bengal in 1772, after Buxar (1764) and the Treaty of Allahabad (1765).

n726f4c6698b.s: The Treaty of Madras (1769) was concluded by the English with:
n726f4c6698b.x: The Treaty of Madras (1769) is associated with Haidar Ali.

n9ee93abbc92.s: Which of the following was NOT a cause of conflict between the English Company and Siraj-ud-Daulah?
o: Fortification of Calcutta without the Nawab's consent
Misuse of dastaks by Company servants
French refusal to obey the Nawab's order to stop fortification
Sheltering of the Nawab's enemies by the Company
n9ee93abbc92.x: The French obeyed the order to stop fortification; it was the English who continued fortifying Calcutta.
